coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Longest substring without repeating characters
coding.question: Given a string S, find the length of the longest substring (a continuous part of S) in which no character appears more than once.
coding.input_format: One line: the string S (no spaces).
coding.output_format: Print the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
coding.constraints: 1 <= length of S <= 100000. S has letters, digits and symbols, but no spaces.
coding.starter_code:
s = input().strip()
# TODO: write your logic here
print(len(s))
hints: Use a sliding window [start, i] that never contains a repeat.
Remember the last index of each character; on a repeat inside the window, move start just past it.
coding.explanation: Move i across the string and keep the last position of each character. If the current character was last seen inside the window, move start past that position. The window length i - start + 1 is a candidate. O(n) time.
coding.label: Candidate-reported

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: 4th highest score without full sorting
coding.question: N participants took a test. Find the 4th highest score without sorting the whole list. Count repeated scores separately: for example, in 90 90 80 70 60 the scores in order are 90, 90, 80, 70, so the 4th highest is 70. If there are fewer than 4 participants, print -1.
coding.input_format:
First line: N.
Second line: N space-separated scores.
coding.output_format: Print the 4th highest score, or -1 if N < 4.
coding.starter_code:
n = int(input())
scores = list(map(int, input().split()))
# TODO: write your logic here
print(-1)
hints: Keep a min-heap that holds only the 4 largest scores seen so far.
The smallest of those 4 is the answer.
coding.explanation: Push each score into a min-heap and pop the smallest whenever the heap has more than 4 items. At the end the heap top is the 4th highest. O(n log 4), which is O(n).
coding.label: Candidate-reported

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Reverse the order of words
coding.question: Given a sentence, print the words in reverse order. The letters inside each word stay the same. For example, sky is beautiful becomes beautiful is sky.
coding.input_format: One line: a sentence of words separated by single spaces.
coding.output_format: Print the words in reverse order, separated by single spaces.
coding.constraints: 1 <= number of words <= 10000. Words contain letters and digits only.
coding.sample_io:
Input:
sky is beautiful
Output:
beautiful is sky

coding.title: Uppercase to lowercase without built-ins

coding.input_format: One line of text. It does not start or end with a space.

coding.title: Distinct values in every window
coding.question: A sensor sends N readings. For every window of K consecutive readings, count how many different values the window has. Print the counts for the windows starting at position 1, 2, ..., N-K+1.
coding.input_format:
First line: N and K.
Second line: N space-separated integers.
coding.output_format: Print N-K+1 counts on one line, separated by spaces.
coding.starter_code:
n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
# TODO: write your logic here
print(" ".join(["0"] * (n - k + 1)))
hints: Slide the window one step at a time: add the new reading, remove the one that left.
Keep a dictionary of counts and delete a key when its count becomes 0; the dictionary size is the answer.
coding.explanation: A dictionary holds counts for the current window. Each step adds one value and removes one, deleting keys that reach 0, so len(dict) is the number of distinct values. O(n) time instead of O(n*k).

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Smallest window containing all characters
coding.question: You are given two strings S and T. Find the length of the smallest substring (continuous part) of S that contains every character of T, including repeats. For example, if T is aab, the window must contain at least two a and one b. If no such window exists, print -1.
coding.input_format:
First line: S.
Second line: T.
coding.output_format: Print the length of the smallest window, or -1.
coding.constraints: 1 <= length of S, T <= 100000. Both strings contain only lowercase letters.
coding.starter_code:
s = input().strip()
t = input().strip()
# TODO: write your logic here
print(-1)
coding.solution:
from collections import Counter
s = input().strip()
t = input().strip()
need = Counter(t)
missing = len(t)
left = 0
best = -1
for right, ch in enumerate(s):
    if need[ch] > 0:
        missing -= 1
    need[ch] -= 1
    while missing == 0:
        length = right - left + 1
        if best == -1 or length < best:
            best = length
        need[s[left]] += 1
        if need[s[left]] > 0:
            missing += 1
        left += 1
print(best)
hints: Expand the right end until the window has everything in T, then shrink from the left while it still does.
Track how many characters of T are still missing instead of comparing whole counters each step.
coding.explanation: need[c] says how many more of c the window needs; missing counts the total still needed. Move right to add characters; when missing hits 0, record the length and move left to shrink. Each index enters and leaves once, so O(|S| + |T|).

coding.subject: Coding
coding.title: Running median of a stream
coding.question: Numbers arrive one by one from a radar feed. After each new number, print the median of all numbers received so far. When the count is even, print the smaller of the two middle numbers (the lower median), so the answer is always one of the numbers.
coding.input_format:
First line: N.
Second line: N space-separated integers in arrival order.
coding.output_format: Print N medians on one line, separated by spaces.
coding.starter_code:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
# TODO: write your logic here
print(" ".join(map(str, a)))
coding.solution:
import heapq
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
low = []   # max-heap (stored as negatives): the smaller half
high = []  # min-heap: the larger half
res = []
for x in a:
    if not low or x <= -low[0]:
        heapq.heappush(low, -x)
    else:
        heapq.heappush(high, x)
    # keep len(low) == len(high) or len(low) == len(high) + 1
    if len(low) > len(high) + 1:
        heapq.heappush(high, -heapq.heappop(low))
    elif len(high) > len(low):
        heapq.heappush(low, -heapq.heappop(high))
    res.append(-low[0])
print(" ".join(map(str, res)))
hints: Keep two heaps: a max-heap for the smaller half and a min-heap for the larger half.
Rebalance so the max-heap has the same size or one more; its top is the lower median.
coding.explanation: The smaller half lives in a max-heap and the larger half in a min-heap. After each insert, move one element across if the sizes differ by more than one. The top of the max-heap is the lower median. O(log n) per number, O(n log n) total, versus O(n^2 log n) for sorting each time.
